publish.title: The machine that changed reading: Gutenberg's press
publish.description: How movable type and the printing press made books cheaper and ideas faster.

scenes.headline: The machine that changed reading
scenes.narration: Five hundred years ago, books were slow and costly to make. One invention changed that.

scenes.headline: Copied by hand
scenes.narration: Before Johannes Gutenberg, every book in Europe was written out by a scribe, slowly, one copy at a time.

scenes.headline: Movable metal type
scenes.narration: Gutenberg, a German craftsman from Mainz, originated printing from movable type. He combined a metal alloy for reusable type, an oil-based ink and a new kind of press.

scenes.headline: From experiment to book
scenes.narration: By 1450 his experiments were refined enough to win a loan. His forty-two line Bible dates from around fourteen fifty to fifty-five. In 1457 a Psalter from Mainz named its printers.

points.text: A Mainz Psalter names its printers

scenes.headline: Books for more people
scenes.narration: The press was considered a history-changing invention, making books widely accessible.

scenes.headline: Hold a book today
scenes.narration: Next time you pick up a book, remember that it was once a rare object.
